subject: knight
reasoning:
I'm planning a detailed humanoid knight model, about 1.85m tall in a relaxed standing pose, working out the joint hierarchy from hips through spine, neck, head, and a separate jaw piece for the helmet visor.

I'm also mapping out arm and leg joint chains (shoulder/elbow/wrist, hip/knee/ankle), establishing world coordinates and key body heights in meters, and sketching how to use the SDK's joint, chain, and part functions to build the spine and neck segments.

Still computing arm joint positions...

Now defining the leg chain with hip, knee, ankle, and toe joints, parented to the hips, and planning to render limbs as tapered sweeps along each chain with varying radius for a metallic armor look.

For armor pieces I'll add discrete parts like boxes and spheres positioned at joints with rotation options, picking a palette of steel, dark steel, gold trim, cloth red, and leather tones, possibly using a mottled paint texture on the steel sweeps for visual variation.

For the torso I'm planning a lofted sweep along the spine chain with stations defined at pelvis, waist, chest, and top heights, each with its own width and depth, and I'm working out how to orient the cross-sections correctly along a vertical path without an explicit up vector.

I'm starting to wonder if it would be safer to just build the torso out of rigid lathe or box pieces attached together instead.

I'll keep the loft for the breastplate's smoothness but use sweeps for limbs. For the armor plating, I'm shaping a scaled sphere for the chest piece, adding a thin ridge box down the center, and a torus belt rotated to lie horizontal at the waist with scaling adjusted to get an elliptical profile. Now I'm figuring out the tasset skirt using a lathe shape for the hip armor.

For the cloth elements, I'm planning a thin box slab as a hanging tabard in front and back, positioning it just outside the lathe skirt's radius with a slight rotation, plus small gold boxes to form a cross emblem on the chest. Next I'm starting on the head, building a bascinet-style helmet from a sphere base.

Still building the helmet pieces...

Now I'm adding a crest plume on top using a catmull curve swept with a tapering radius, attached rigidly to the head bone, plus a vertical nose guard ridge at the front. For the shoulders, I'm placing scaled sphere pauldrons rigged to shoulder joints, with a torus rim detail considered for the lower edge.

I'm filling in the rest of the armor set: a small cone spike on the helmet, gold elbow cops, boxy mitten-style gauntlets with a simple thumb, dark-soled boots, knee cops, and swept cuisses along the leg chain. For the leg geometry I'm working out a tapering radius function across the hip-to-ankle span so the thigh, knee, and shin thickness blend smoothly based on position along the sweep.

For the arms I'm setting up a similar radius taper from shoulder to wrist, plus a steel vambrace capsule over the forearm. I'm adding a scabbarded sword at the hip with a slanted grip, cross guard, and gold pommel, and a kite shield strapped to the opposite forearm using an extruded outline with a gold cross emblem and boss, positioning it so it clears the pauldron and leg armor.

I'm also designing a cloth cape as an extruded outline tilted backward from the shoulders, working out the angle and depth so it falls behind the body without clipping through the skirt armor, plus a gold hem torus at the skirt's bottom edge, a neck gorget cylinder, and a short neck-to-head joint chain. I'm planning to use a steel mottle paint for the torso and limb sweeps while keeping simpler flat colors for smaller parts, and writing helper functions for parts, boxes, and spheres so geometry stays fresh and avoids accidental sharing issues. Now I'm finalizing the full part list -- pauldrons with ridge spikes, waist belt and buckle, sabaton boots with rounded toes, hand boxes aligned to forearm direction, and a thumb capsule -- before writing out the complete generation code.
